author: sonnet
label: climb-05-01
changes: Added terms for job queue and storage helpers (Q1, Q2) and a line on how a large file reaches the user (Q4).
Step 1: said how the page tells a CSV 200 from a 202 and what it does with each (Q3).
Step 3a: said the server counts rows and elapsed time while paging, and that the user sees a normal queued state on fallback (Q5).
Step 5: a revoked permission now marks the export failed and returns without retrying, with no email, instead of raising and retrying (Q7). Step 9 stops if already failed. Added a matching test.
Step 7: stated that a zero-row conditional update is fine and the handler continues to Step 8 (Q8).
Retries section: one line on when the queue starts the next attempt (Q6).
Added open questions on bucket access (Q2) and queue failure detection (Q6).
Added a opening summary paragraph stating how the reports page and rows API work today, then the main flow and why it is shaped this way.
Moved all terms and decisions into one Terms section and expanded the job queue term: attempts, backoff, timeout, no saved progress, who calls on_final_failure, at-least-once delivery.
Added definitions for Replica and the bucket lifecycle rule (the only cleanup), and why the exports table in the primary does not break the replica-only rule.
Reformatted every step with the same four parts: what starts it, what it does, data kept, if it fails.
Gave the reason for keyset paging (row_id unique and increasing) in the step where it first appears; Step 6 now refers back to Step 3a instead of repeating the query.
Stated in Step 3a the 40 s deadline reason (API killed at 60 s) and where the row count and elapsed time are checked.
Added Step 1 detail on how the page tells a CSV response from a 202, and in Terms that large files come only by email link with no download button.
Step 5 revoked-permission branch: no retry, no on_final_failure, no email, page shows the error; Step 9 stops if already failed or done.
Step 7 states that a zero-row conditional update is fine and the handler still proceeds to Step 8.
Added a failure summary table so failure handling is visible in one place.
Cut the repeated 'why the job fits' retry wording down to two short bullets; trimmed duplicated explanations of the half-written-file guarantee and stale-upload cleanup.
Removed the interior cross-reference codes in favour of plain step names; kept the open questions at the end, unchanged in substance.
holes: Q2: Where does the `exports` bucket live and who can read it? What are `start_multipart`, `upload_part`, `complete_multipart`, `signed_url`: a storage service or your own helpers? (author: storage.py says the exports bucket exists and the four functions are our existing helpers around the object store (start_multipart, upload_part, complete_multipart, signed_url are all in that file). Who can read the bucket directly is not stated anywhere; the plan assumes downloads go only through signed links. Added a term line and an open question.)

Q6: Step 9 says the final failure can be a timeout or worker death. How does the queue detect these and decide an attempt is over, and does it start the next attempt only after that? (author: jobs.py says an attempt fails if the handler raises, hits the 1800 s timeout, or the worker dies, and a failed attempt is retried after the backoff. It does not say how the queue detects a dead worker. The next attempt starts only after the backoff following a failed attempt. Added an open question and one line in the retries section.)
